WK-A-LAB-1.title: LAB: PC Building: Computer System Assembly
WK-A-LAB-1.algorithmIntro: This process explains how the main components of a computer system are assembled and connected in the correct order. It shows how input components, processing components, output components, and storage components are installed to create a working computer system.

steps.title: Install the Power Supply
Install the CPU>>1: Add text: CPU Is Installed as the Main Processing Component
Install the RAM>>1: Connect Power Supply → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: RAM Provides Temporary Working Memory for the CPU
Install the SSD>>1: Connect Power Supply → SSD: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: SSD Stores the Operating System, Programs, and Files
Install the GPU>>1: Connect Power Supply → GPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: GPU Processes Graphics for the Display
Connect the Monitor>>1: Connect GPU → Monitor: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Monitor Receives the Computer's Visual Output
Connect the Keyboard>>1: Connect Keyboard → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Keyboard Provides User Input to the Computer
Connect the Mouse>>1: Connect Mouse → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Mouse Provides User Pointing and Selection Input
Check All Connections>>1: Connect Power Supply → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: All Main Components Are Connected
Complete the Computer System>>1: Add text: The Computer System Is Fully Assembled and Ready to Start

WK-A-LAB-1.finalCheck: Power Supply → CPU → RAM → SSD → GPU → Monitor → Keyboard → Mouse

WK-A-LAB-2.title: LAB: CPU:Instruction Processing
WK-A-LAB-2.algorithmIntro: This process explains how the CPU receives, fetches, decodes, and executes a computer instruction. It shows how registers, the instruction decoder, cache, RAM, and ALU work together to process the required data. The purpose is to make the instruction-processing sequence clear from the keyboard input through CPU execution to the final result on the monitor.

steps.title: Enter a Command
Fetch the Instruction>>1: Connect Keyboard → Instruction Fetch Unit: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Fetches the Instruction You Entered
Load the Instruction>>1: Connect Instruction Fetch Unit → Registers: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Instruction Loaded into the CPU Registers
Decode the Instruction>>1: Connect Registers → Instruction Decoder: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Decoder Determines the Required Operation
Check Fast Data>>1: Connect Instruction Decoder → Cache: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Checks Cache for Any Needed Data
Fetch Missing Data>>1: Connect Cache → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: RAM Supplies Data When It Is Not in Cache
Execute the Operation>>1: Connect RAM → ALU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: ALU Performs the Calculation
Display the Result>>1: Connect ALU → Monitor: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Monitor Shows the Calculated Answer

WK-A-LAB-2.finalCheck: Keyboard → Instruction Fetch Unit → Registers → Instruction Decoder → Cache → RAM → ALU → Monitor

WK-A-LAB-3.title: LAB: RAM: Data Access
WK-A-LAB-3.algorithmIntro: This process explains how data requested by an application is retrieved from RAM and made available for use. It shows how the CPU registers, memory controller, memory bus, RAM module, and cache cooperate during data access. The purpose is to trace the data path from the user's file-opening action through memory components to the displayed file contents.

steps.title: Open a File
Request the Data>>1: Connect Mouse → Registers: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Registers Request the File Data
Contact the Memory Controller>>1: Connect Registers → Memory Controller: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Memory Controller Receives the Request
Address the Memory Location>>1: Connect Memory Controller → Memory Bus: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Memory Address Is Sent Across the Memory Bus
Access the RAM Module>>1: Connect Memory Bus → RAM Module: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: RAM Module Retrieves the Requested Data
Cache the Data>>1: Connect RAM Module → Cache: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Data Is Cached for Faster Future Access
Display the File>>1: Connect Cache → Monitor: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Monitor Displays the File Contents

WK-A-LAB-3.finalCheck: Mouse → Registers → Memory Controller → Memory Bus → RAM Module → Cache → Monitor

WK-2-LAB-1.title: LAB: RAM: CPU Reads Data
WK-2-LAB-1.algorithmIntro: This process explains how the CPU retrieves data from RAM when the required data is not already available in the CPU Cache. It shows how the memory request, location identification, data transfer, and CPU register loading work together so the CPU can use the retrieved data to execute an instruction.

steps.title: Install the Power Supply
Load the Operating System>>1: Connect Power Supply → Operating System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Operating System Receives Power to Begin Loading
Load Data into RAM>>1: Connect Operating System → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Operating System Loads the Program and Its Data into RAM
Execute the Instruction>>1: Connect RAM → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Executes an Instruction Requiring Data from RAM
Check the CPU Cache>>1: Connect CPU → CPU Cache: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Cache Is Checked for the Required Data
Send Request to Memory Controller>>1: Connect CPU Cache → Memory Controller: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Sends a Memory-Read Request Since Data Is Not in Cache
Identify the RAM Location>>1: Connect Memory Controller → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Memory Controller Identifies the Required Location in RAM
Transfer Data Across the Memory Bus>>1: Connect RAM → Memory Bus: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Requested Data Is Transferred Through the Memory Bus
Load Data into CPU Register>>1: Connect Memory Bus → CPU Register: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Data Is Placed into a CPU Register for Immediate Use
Use the Data>>1: Connect CPU Register → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Uses the Data to Execute the Instruction

WK-2-LAB-1.finalCheck: Power Supply → Operating System → RAM → CPU → CPU Cache → Memory Controller → RAM → Memory Bus → CPU Register → CPU

WK-2-LAB-2.title: LAB: RAM: CPU Writes Data
WK-2-LAB-2.algorithmIntro: This process explains how the CPU stores newly produced data in RAM. It shows how the CPU register, memory controller, memory bus, and RAM cooperate so that data is written to the correct memory location and the CPU cache is updated accordingly.

steps.title: Install the Power Supply
Load the Operating System>>1: Connect Power Supply → Operating System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Operating System Starts Up After Receiving Power
Execute the Instruction>>1: Connect Operating System → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Executes an Instruction That Produces Data to Store
Place Data in CPU Register>>1: Connect CPU → CPU Register: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Resulting Data Is Placed in a CPU Register
Send Write Request to Memory Controller>>1: Connect CPU Register → Memory Controller: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Sends a Memory-Write Request with Data and Target Location
Transfer Data Across the Memory Bus>>1: Connect Memory Controller → Memory Bus: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Memory Controller Identifies the Location and Sends Data Across the Bus
Store Data in RAM>>1: Connect Memory Bus → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: RAM Stores the Data in the Selected Memory Location
Update the CPU Cache>>1: Connect RAM → CPU Cache: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Cache Is Updated According to the Cache-Management Method
Continue Execution>>1: Connect CPU Cache → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Continues with the Next Instruction

WK-2-LAB-2.finalCheck: Power Supply → Operating System → CPU → CPU Register → Memory Controller → Memory Bus → RAM → CPU Cache → CPU

WK-2-LAB-3.title: LAB: SSD: CPU Reads a File
WK-2-LAB-3.algorithmIntro: This process explains how a computer retrieves a file stored on an SSD and makes it available to the CPU. It shows the complete path from the user's file-opening request through the SSD controller and flash memory, into RAM, and through the CPU cache to the final result on the monitor.

steps.title: Install the Power Supply
Load the Operating System>>1: Connect Power Supply → Operating System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Operating System Receives the User's Request to Open a File
Execute the Request>>1: Connect Operating System → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Executes the Operating System Instructions for the File Request
Send the Storage Request>>1: Connect CPU → Storage Interface: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Sends a Storage-Read Request Through the Storage Interface
Locate the Data>>1: Connect Storage Interface → SSD Controller: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: SSD Controller Determines Where the Requested Data Is Stored
Retrieve the Data>>1: Connect SSD Controller → SSD Flash Memory: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: SSD Flash Memory Retrieves the Required Data
Transfer the Data Back>>1: Connect SSD Flash Memory → Storage Interface: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: SSD Transfers the Data Through the Storage Interface
Place the File into RAM>>1: Connect Storage Interface → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Received File Data Is Placed into RAM
Retrieve Data via Memory Controller>>1: Connect RAM → Memory Controller: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Retrieves the Required Data from RAM Through the Memory Controller
Pass Through CPU Cache>>1: Connect Memory Controller → CPU Cache: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Data Passes Through the CPU Cache as Applicable
Process the Data>>1: Connect CPU Cache → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Processes the Retrieved Data
Display the Result>>1: Connect CPU → Monitor: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: CPU Sends the Result to the Monitor

WK-2-LAB-3.finalCheck: Power Supply → Operating System → CPU → Storage Interface → SSD Controller → SSD Flash Memory → Storage Interface → RAM → Memory Controller → CPU Cache → CPU → Monitor

WK-C-LAB-1.title: LAB: Virtual Memory: CPU Requests Data
WK-C-LAB-1.algorithmIntro: This process explains how a computer retrieves data for the CPU when the requested data is not already available in RAM. It shows how the Operating System, secondary storage, RAM, memory controller, memory bus, and CPU cache cooperate to locate and deliver the data the CPU needs. The purpose is to trace the complete path from the CPU's request through virtual memory to the data being used.

steps.title: Install the Power Supply
Load the Operating System>>1: Connect Power Supply → Operating System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Loads a Program and Allocates Memory Space for It
Execute the Instruction>>1: Connect Operating System → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The CPU Executes an Instruction That Needs Specific Data
Check RAM for the Data>>1: Connect CPU → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Checks Whether the Data Is Already Stored in RAM

Locate the Data in Secondary Storage>>1: Connect RAM → Secondary Storage: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Since the Data Is Not in RAM, the Operating System Finds It on Secondary Storage
Copy the Data into RAM>>1: Connect Secondary Storage → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Required Data Is Copied from Secondary Storage into RAM
Locate the Data in RAM>>1: Connect RAM → Memory Controller: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Memory Controller Finds the Exact Location of the Data in RAM
Transfer Data Across the Memory Bus>>1: Connect Memory Controller → Memory Bus: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Data Is Transferred Through the Memory Bus Toward the CPU
Store Data in the CPU Cache>>1: Connect Memory Bus → CPU Cache: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The CPU Cache May Store a Copy of the Data for Faster Future Access
Use the Data>>1: Connect CPU Cache → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The CPU Uses the Data to Complete the Instruction

WK-C-LAB-1.finalCheck: Power Supply → Operating System → Secondary Storage → RAM → Memory Controller → Memory Bus → CPU Cache → CPU

WK-C-LAB-2.title: LAB: Process Creation: Starting a New Program
WK-C-LAB-2.algorithmIntro: This process explains how a computer starts a new program when the user opens it. It shows how the Operating System, storage, RAM, and the waiting list work together to load the program and prepare it to run on the CPU. The purpose is to make the full sequence clear from opening the program to the CPU executing its instructions.
WK-C-LAB-2.flowchartTitle: LAB:Process Creation: Starting a New Program

steps.title: Install the Power Supply
Open the Program>>1: Connect Power Supply → Operating System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The User Opens a Program and the Operating System Begins Processing the Request
Locate the Program Files>>1: Connect Operating System → Storage: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Finds the Program's Files in Storage
Load the Program into RAM>>1: Connect Storage → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Loads the Program into RAM
Set Up Program Information>>1: Add text: The Operating System Sets Up the Basic Information the Program Needs to Run
Place the Program in the Waiting List>>1: Connect RAM → Waiting List: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The New Program Is Placed in a Waiting List Along with Other Programs
Check the Waiting List>>1: Connect Waiting List → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The CPU Checks the Waiting List for the Next Program to Run
Run the Program>>1: Add text: The CPU Begins Running the New Program's Instructions
Use RAM While Running>>1: Connect CPU → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Program Uses RAM to Store Data While It Runs
Continue or Finish Execution>>1: Add text: The Program Continues Running Until It Is Finished, Paused, or Closed

WK-C-LAB-2.finalCheck: Power Supply → Operating System → Storage → RAM → Waiting List → CPU

WK-C-LAB-3.title: LAB: Process Switching: Between Programs
WK-C-LAB-3.algorithmIntro: This process explains how a computer pauses one running program and starts another. It shows how the Operating System saves and restores program information so the CPU can switch between Program A and Program B smoothly. The purpose is to trace the sequence of pausing, saving, and resuming that keeps multiple programs running on a single CPU.

steps.title: Install the Power Supply
Run Program A on the CPU>>1: Add text: The CPU Is Currently Running Program A
Receive a Request for Program B>>1: Connect CPU (Program A) → Operating System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Receives a Request to Run Program B
Pause Program A>>1: Connect Operating System → CPU (Program A): Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Pauses Program A
Save Program A's Information>>1: Connect Operating System → Saved Program Information: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Information About Program A Is Saved So It Can Continue Later
Select Program B to Run>>1: Add text: The Operating System Selects Program B to Run Next
Load Program B's Information>>1: Connect Saved Program Information → CPU (Program B): Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: Saved Information About Program B Is Loaded
Run Program B on the CPU>>1: Add text: The CPU Begins Running Program B
Keep Program A Saved>>1: Add text: Program A Stays Saved Until It Is Chosen Again
Continue Switching Between Programs>>1: Add text: The CPU Continues Switching Between Programs As Needed

WK-C-LAB-3.finalCheck: CPU (Program A) → Operating System → Saved Program Information → CPU (Program B)

WK-D-LAB-1.title: LAB: File Management: Opening a File
WK-D-LAB-1.algorithmIntro: This process explains how a computer opens a file when the user clicks on it. It shows how the Operating System, storage, RAM, and CPU work together to find the matching program, load it, and display the file's contents. The purpose is to trace the complete sequence from the user's click to the file appearing on the screen.

steps.title: Click on the File
Check the File Type>>1: Connect Mouse → Operating System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Checks the File's Type>>3: Type Command: open
Find the Matching Program>>1: Connect Operating System → Program: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Finds the Matching Program to Open the File
Load the Program into RAM>>1: Connect Program → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Matching Program Is Loaded into RAM So It Can Run
Run the Program>>1: Connect RAM → CPU: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The CPU Begins Running the Program
Open the Program on the Screen>>1: Connect CPU → Monitor: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Program Opens on the Screen
Locate the File's Data>>1: Connect Operating System → Storage: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Loads the File's Data from Storage
Retrieve the File's Data>>1: Connect Storage → File: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The File's Data Is Retrieved from Storage
Display the File's Data>>1: Connect File → Monitor: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The File's Data Appears Inside the Program on the Screen
View the File>>1: Add text: The User Can Now View or Use the File
Keep the File Open>>1: Add text: The File Stays Open Until the User Closes It

WK-D-LAB-1.finalCheck: Mouse → Operating System → Program → RAM → CPU → Storage → File → Monitor

WK-D-LAB-2.title: LAB: File Management: Creating a New Folder
WK-D-LAB-2.algorithmIntro: This process explains how a computer creates a new folder. It shows how the Operating System works with the keyboard, storage, and the current directory to name, create, and save the new folder. The purpose is to make the full sequence clear from choosing to make a folder to it being ready to store files.
WK-D-LAB-2.flowchartTitle: LAB:File Management: Creating a New Folder

steps.title: Choose to Make a New Folder
Request a Folder Name>>1: Connect Mouse → Operating System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Asks for a Folder Name
Type the Folder Name>>1: Connect Keyboard → Operating System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The User Types a Name for the Folder
Create the Folder>>1: Connect Operating System → New Folder: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Creates the Folder>>3: Type Command: mkdir
Save the Folder to Storage>>1: Connect New Folder → Storage: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The New Folder Is Saved to Storage
Display the New Folder>>1: Connect New Folder → Monitor: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The New Folder Appears on the Screen
Add the Folder to the Directory>>1: Connect New Folder → Directory: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Folder Is Added to the Current Directory
Prepare the Folder for Files>>1: Add text: The Folder Is Now Ready to Store Files
Open the Folder to Add Files>>1: Add text: The User Can Open the Folder to Add Files

WK-D-LAB-2.finalCheck: Mouse → Keyboard → Operating System → New Folder → Storage → Monitor → Directory

WK-D-LAB-3.title: LAB: User Accounts: Logging In
WK-D-LAB-3.algorithmIntro: This process explains how a computer handles a user login. It shows how the Operating System checks the entered details against saved account information, then loads the user's account, desktop, and files. The purpose is to trace the complete sequence from entering a username and password to the desktop appearing on the screen.

steps.title: Enter Username and Password
Check the Login Details>>1: Connect Keyboard → Operating System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Checks the Username and Password>>3: Type Command: login

Compare to Saved Account Information>>1: Connect Operating System → Saved Account Information: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Compares Them to Saved Account Information
Allow Access>>1: Connect Saved Account Information → Operating System: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: If the Details Are Correct, Access Is Allowed
Open the User's Account>>1: Connect Operating System → Account: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Operating System Opens the User's Account
Load the Desktop and Files>>1: Connect Account → Storage: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Desktop and Files Load from Storage for That User
Prepare the Desktop in Memory>>1: Connect Storage → RAM: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Desktop Environment Is Loaded into RAM
Display the Desktop>>1: Connect RAM → Monitor: Line Type: Arrow Connection Line>>2: Add text: The Desktop Appears on the Screen
Use the Computer>>1: Add text: The User Can Now Use the Computer
Stay Logged In>>1: Add text: The Account Stays Open Until the User Logs Out

WK-D-LAB-3.finalCheck: Keyboard → Operating System → Saved Account Information → Account → Storage → RAM → Monitor
